text:
maggie: Customer reported tool call failures for OCR tool when sending large image blobs (~70-120KB). They're seeing SchemaValidationError: "tool_args malformed". Says py/ts/go SDKs act differently around the 64KB boundary. Any ideas? :thinking_face:

sanjay: Paste the raw error + a tiny repro and which model/route.

maggie: Route /v1/infer/toolcall pinned to rwd-llama-mini. Error snippet: "SchemaValidationError: expected object for 'tool_args', got string". Server logs show args payload with extra quoting and embedded � markers. Minimal repro below.

maggie: ```python
# minimal repro (py)
from redwood import Client
cli = Client()
img = open('sample.png','rb').read()
res = cli.call_tool('image_ocr', args={'image_bytes': img})
```

eli: That pattern suggests bytes got str()-ed instead of being base64-encoded properly. What do server-side raw bodies look like?

maggie: Received body: "{\"image_bytes\": \"b'\\x89PNG...\\x00\\x00'\"}" i.e. leading b'...' wrapper inside a JSON string.

kevin: Sounds like one of the serializers called repr(bytes) during chunked upload. Which SDK versions?

maggie: Py 1.2.8, TS 0.6.7, Go 0.4.2. Customer tested all three.

ryan: I ran quick local tests: all three fail but with different final encodings. Py: repr(bytes) inserted. TS: double-quoted base64 chunks (escaped quotes). Go: bytes -> base64 -> re-marshaled so you get double-encoding. Common trigger: crossing our 65536 internal chunk boundary.

sanjay: Repro steps for engineers: upload a ~80KB PNG, or force chunk_size=32768 in SDK client. Below threshold everything is fine. So chunker+serializer interaction is the culprit.

devex: Customer impact summary: about 20% of OCR tool calls failing after they ramped image sizes yesterday. Some requests retried, causing latency spikes. Billing unaffected but poor UX.

kevin: Short-term options: ask customer to set chunk_size to a large value or disable chunking if possible; provide staging RCs for SDKs; or add a tolerant server-side normalizer that strips leading b'...' or unquotes extra-quoted base64.

sanjay: I'll draft SDK fixes: py: ensure chunker returns raw bytes and base64.b64encode is used, never repr(); ts: ensure chunk pieces are plain strings (no additional JSON.stringify wrappers); go: stop double json.Marshal on assembled chunks.

maggie: Can you add an automated smoke test that uploads a 100KB file and asserts server receives a JSON object with image_bytes as a base64 string (no b' prefix, no wrapped quotes)?

sanjay: Yes, adding tests in py/ts/go SDK suites and a CI job to exercise chunk boundaries.

support-bot: cut rc builds: py-sdk 1.2.9-rc1, ts-sdk 0.6.8-rc1 published to staging. :shipit:

maggie: Customer tried py 1.2.9-rc1 on staging: they report no more SchemaValidationError. Asking for prod release asap.

kevin: We'll push a temporary server-side parser that normalizes malformed cases and emits a metric 'malformed_tool_args_detected'. This buys time while SDKs propagate. Also adding a small guard in server parse to reject any payload starting with b' after mitigation tests pass.

devex: Added changelog blurb for SDKs explaining chunking/serialization mismatch and recommended upgrades and a short migration note for customers sending binary payloads.

eli: After prod roll we need to run full regression: send a mix of sizes 1KB..200KB across pinned models and confirm no schema errors and no double-encoded payloads are logged.

ryan: PRs opened: py#432, ts#433, go#434; tests included. CI pending.

maggie: Customer loop closed: offered workaround (use rc or bump chunk_size), customer appreciated the fast triage and will watch for prod rollout tomorrow morning PT. :thumbsup:

sanjay: Follow-ups: merge PRs after green CI, cut stable releases, and instrument server logs for remaining malformed cases.

maggie: Marking thread resolved once stable SDK releases are published and server-side tolerant parser removed. Thanks team! :smile:
